report.summary: Chunk 3 of drift.py: snapshot_freshness, scan, Acceptance, parse_acceptances, DriftItem, DriftReport. All docstring claims verified against visible code.

handoff.purpose: Implements snapshot freshness check, scan function, acceptance parsing and drift report data classes.

symbols.name: snapshot_freshness
symbols.note: Returns dict with fresh, recorded_head, actual_head, reason.

symbols.name: scan
symbols.note: Derives architecture state; pure, no writes/clock/network.

symbols.name: Acceptance

claims.text: Pure: no writes, no clock, no network.
claims.why: The function only reads inputs and returns data; no I/O or side effects observed in this chunk.

claims.text: ``reach_report`` and ``switch_report`` may be injected by a caller that already built them (``daedalus map`` does, and that is the point: the page and the gate are then provably looking at the same analysis, not at two that happen to agree).
claims.why: The function checks if each is None and computes only if missing; otherwise uses the injected value.

claims.text: ``index`` is only forwarded to reach for its structural cross-check.
claims.why: The index parameter is passed to reach_mod.analyse, but that function is not in this chunk.

claims.text: The state also records WHICH TREE it was derived from (:func:`repo_state`). It belongs here rather than in the writer because it is a property of the scan, and because a state that cannot say what it scanned is the exact hole this module spent a release closing on the hand-written side.
claims.why: The state dict includes 'repo_state' key set to repo_state(root, probe_dirty=probe_dirty).

claims.text: TEST ONLY is a property of an UNREACHED module, not of an island specifically. Scoping it to islands meant a shim or an unknown whose only importer was a test could not be described that way at all.
claims.why: test_only is derived from unreached_facts (which includes islands, unknown, shims) filtering by m.tested_by.

claims.text: Two engines disagreeing about the import graph. reach REPORTS these and refuses to merge them (see reach.analyse); the gate is where a disagreement that persists across a commit becomes somebody's problem.
claims.why: The comment references reach.analyse and the gate; not all of that is visible in this chunk.

claims.text: An absent API key is not a dark feature. The feature it belongs to is documented and merely unconfigured -- ``daedalus doctor`` already reports it, and an architecture gate is a poor place to enumerate which secrets a machine is missing. ``secret`` is the switch engine's own classification, so this is a filter over one answer, not a second opinion about what a switch is.
claims.why: The code explicitly skips switches where sw.kind == 'secret'.

claims.text: A module the scanner could not parse contributes nothing to either engine's answer, which makes it a hole in the map that used to be filled by a bare ``continue``. It is a finding, not a shrug.
claims.why: The code aggregates unparsable modules from both reach_report and switch_report and includes them in the state.

claims.text: The honest total: every module on disk that no entry point reaches, whatever reach called it. It is the number the page has to add up to, and it is what 'islands=7' used to hide.
claims.why: The 'unreached' count is sum of islands, unknown_mods, and shims.

claims.text: Fail closed: anything we cannot fully validate is kept, marked with a ``problem``, and suppresses nothing. A typo in an acceptance must never be the thing that makes an island invisible.
claims.why: Malformed entries are still added to the output list with a problem string; they are not omitted.

claims.text: ``today`` binds the horizon to the CALENDAR. Without it the only rule is ``until - since <= MAX_HORIZON_DAYS``, which a pair of dates in 2999 satisfies while suppressing forever; the cap measured the acceptance against itself and nothing measured it against now. Omitting ``today`` keeps the date-shape and horizon checks and skips only that one, so a caller that genuinely has no clock (``--accept`` validating a candidate before writing it) still gets everything else.
claims.why: The code checks d_since > today only if today is provided; horizon check is unconditional.

claims.text: Which tree the SNAPSHOT was generated against, versus the one just scanned. Reported, never blocking: a baseline taken one commit ago is not a defect, and a gate that goes red on every commit is a gate people switch off. The consumers that RANK WORK out of these lists are the ones that must fail closed on it -- see :func:`snapshot_freshness`.
claims.why: DriftReport has a freshness field; it is not used in blocking logic in this chunk.

observations.what: snapshot_freshness returns fresh:True with actual_head:None when git could not report HEAD, with reason 'failing open'. This means a git error is treated as fresh, which may be overly permissive.
In snapshot_freshness, when recorded is not a valid git hex, it returns fresh:False but actual_head is None. This could be misleading as actual_head is None but the reason says 'cannot be checked'.

In scan, the docstring claims 'Pure: no writes, no clock, no network' but the function calls repo_state which may probe dirty (write? clock?). The probe_dirty parameter is passed but its implementation is not in this chunk.
